learning_objective: 🎯 Unleash your imagination! Learn how to recall visual details from memory and arrange them creatively into a beautiful, balanced artwork.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Memory drawing involves recalling an event, a place, or an everyday scene (like a busy market, a rainy day, or a festival) from your past and drawing it without looking at a reference.
Composition is how you arrange elements (people, objects, background) inside your paper. A good composition guides the viewer's eye smoothly across the entire artwork.
Every artwork needs a focal point—the most important part of the drawing where you want the viewer to look first. You can create it using bright colors, larger sizes, or placement.
Balance means visual weight is evenly distributed. Symmetrical balance is like a mirror image. Asymmetrical balance is having different objects of equal visual weight on both sides.
A great creative composition tells a story. By adding facial expressions, action, and background details, your drawing can communicate emotions and narratives to the viewer.

fun_activity.title: 🧠 The 30-Second Glance
fun_activity.instructions: Look at an interesting picture or a messy room for exactly 30 seconds. Close your eyes, turn away, and draw everything you can remember on a piece of paper. Check back to see how many details your memory retained!

exam_tips: 📌 Always sketch a light layout of your entire composition before detailing any single object.
📌 Use the 'Rule of Thirds': place your focal point off-center to make the composition more dynamic and interesting.
📌 In memory drawing, focus on capturing the overall mood and action of the scene, rather than minute details.
quick_recap: ⭐ Memory drawing strengthens your observation skills and visual recall in daily life.
⭐ Overlapping objects and varying their sizes creates a sense of depth in your composition.
⭐ Asymmetrical balance often looks more natural and interesting than perfect symmetrical balance.
